page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, two woodcut medallions (coins) side by side: left with the head of Osiris, right with the head of Isis. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Text block below in one column. Below the text, a woodcut ornament. Signature at lower right.

main_text.p: OSIRIS, Camesenui & Rheae filius, imperauit Aegyptiis annis 35. Hic Rex magnus, & pro Deo habitus est: hic, anno mundi 2008. ante Christum natum 1954. qui erat annus nonus regni Zameis Niniae, Regis Babylonis, inuētis à se & sorore adolescentula frumēto, & frugibus, cœpit docere illa in Palæstina. inde reuerfus in Aegyptum, & inuēto aratro, & his quae ad agriculturam pertinebant, sensim vniuersum peragrauit orbem, docens quæcunque inuenerat: & ita vniuerso imperauit orbi, exceptis gentibus quae iam in Babyloniorum venerāt potestatem. Vide Bero.lib.5.
ISIS maxima, dicta etiā Iuno Aegyptia, soror & vxor Osi-ridis, magni apud Aegyptios nominis extitit: testatur eius epitaphium in columna, in hæc verba olim sculptum:

l.i: Ego Isis sum Aegypti regina à ☿Mercurio erudita.
Quæ ego legibus statui, nullus soluet.
Ego sum in astro Canis refulgens.
Gaude, gaude Aegypte, quae me nutristi.

main_text.p: Plura qui volet, legat primum & secundum librum Diodori Siculi, de fabulo.antiq.gestis.

page.notes: Medallion left: legend around the head reads approximately "OSIRIS R..." and "ARGIV..." (partly illegible, not transcribed). Medallion right: legend reads approximately "ISIS IVNO" and "AEGYPT..." (partly illegible). These are part of the woodcut and are described here, not transcribed as text. The inscription's "Mercurio" is preceded by a planetary sign (drawn like ☿), and "Mihi" has a similar sign before it; both are transcribed as printed or as the nearest Unicode sign. The woodcut ornament below the text is not text. The "Q" opening "Quæ" in the inscription is a decorated initial.
